task.description: FIXED in dado main 105f8f9. batten-core annotated LexicalScope::language with #[serde(with = "dado_core::language_serde")] while the local dado-core (patched in .cargo/config.toml) had no such module, so batten-core could not compile at all - the reference outlived its module. Restored as a self-contained adapter over the five-variant miter_engine::Language with canonical lowercase names and rs/ts/js/py aliases; the thirteen-format From conversions do not apply to that type. Verified: batten-core check --all-targets is clean. Root cause worth noting: no gate has run over batten recently, which is exactly what outfeed gate now prevents.
task.title: dado-core lost language_serde, leaving batten-core unbuildable

receipt.summary: Fixed on dado main at 105f8f9: batten-core referenced dado_core::language_serde while the locally patched dado-core had no such module, so batten could not compile. The adapter is restored as a self-contained mapping over miter_engine::Language - the five-variant AST language, for which the thirteen-format From conversions in miter-engine do not apply - serialising canonical lowercase names and accepting the rs/ts/js/py aliases. Verified by cargo check -p batten-core --all-targets, which is now clean. Surfaced while promoting the telemetry record for JN-4; the fact that two members were uncompilable confirms the value of outfeed gate covering every repository.

events.description: CORRECTION to the original record, which claimed dado-core had lost the module. git log --all -- "*language_serde*" shows it has never existed in this repository in any commit except the one that adds it - there is no deletion to point at, and no published dado-core in the local registry. So this was not a removal that forgot its dependents: batten-core has carried an annotation naming a module nobody ever wrote, which means batten has not been compiled since that annotation landed. Restored in dado main 105f8f9 as a self-contained mapping over the five-variant miter_engine::Language (which derives no serde traits), serialising canonical lowercase names and accepting rs/ts/js/py aliases; cargo check -p batten-core --all-targets is clean. OPEN QUESTION deliberately left to the owner: the cleaner long-term fix is to drop the adapter and type LexicalScope::language as gaugeblock_contracts::Language, which already owns canonical lowercase serde plus lenient aliases per GB-143, converting to the miter taxonomy at the boundary. That is a wire-contract decision, so it is tracked as a follow-up rather than folded into a bug fix.
events.title: batten-core referenced a dado_core::language_serde module that has never existed

events.description: TRUE HISTORY, corrected twice. First record claimed dado lost the module; wrong. Second claimed it never existed; also wrong, and it caused a shim to be restored that resurrected deliberately deleted code. The pickaxe (git log -S language_serde) finds the truth: dado commit c88b13c, "refactor(dado-core): consume gaugeblock-contracts and drop the language shim", the fourth staged repoint under the GB-143 option-A decision, deleted dado 36-line language_serde module on purpose because gaugeblock-contracts Language already spells languages in the lowercase form the committed packs use and reads them leniently. That repoint did not sweep the other repositories, so batten-core kept #[serde(with = "dado_core::language_serde")] on LexicalScope::language against a module that no longer existed, and batten has not compiled since - with no gate running over it to notice. My first fix restored the shim (reverted in dado 8ef0d59). The correct fix is now in batten a1c8381: type the field as gaugeblock-contracts Language and drop the annotation, with one construction site in scope_filter.rs and one test import following. cargo check -p batten-core --all-targets is clean. Process lesson: a string search by file path misses inline modules; the pickaxe search is what finds removals, and every repoint under GB-143 should have swept dependents across all repositories.
events.title: batten-core carried a serde annotation for a module dado deleted on purpose

receipt.summary: Corrected and re-verified. The true cause is dado c88b13c (GB-143 option-A repoint), which deliberately deleted dado 36-line language_serde module because gaugeblock-contracts Language already serialises canonical lowercase names and reads leniently. That repoint did not sweep the other repositories, so batten-core annotations outlived the module and batten has not compiled since, with no gate running over it. My first attempt restored the shim and was reverted in dado 8ef0d59; the correct fix is batten a1c8381, which types LexicalScope::language as gaugeblock-contracts Language and drops the annotation (the field is pure wire data - batten-core has no .language call site), with one construction site and one test import following. cargo check -p batten-core --all-targets is clean. Lesson recorded on the ticket: path-based git log misses inline modules, the pickaxe git log -S finds removals, and every GB-143 repoint needed a cross-repository dependent sweep.
